extracted.intended_audience: Program Chairs / conference organizers using OpenReview to run paper matching and assignments
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and operational requirements for computing/uploading affinity scores and computing conflicts in OpenReview's Paper Matching Setup, and for preparing groups (Senior ACs, ACs, Reviewers) and profiles prior to automated matching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setup Matching prerequisite
rubrics_metrics.description: The Setup Matching is the first step needed to make assignments between Senior Area Chairs, Area Chairs, Reviewers and submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once this step is completed you can run the Matching following the instructions. The 'Paper Matching Setup' feature must be used before running automated matching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of Paper Matching Setup
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper Matching Setup is enabled for any venue and the button is activated once the Submission Deadline (or Abstract Deadline, if there is one) has passed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can find the 'Paper Matching Setup' button on your venue request form. The button will become available after the submission deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single concurrent setup restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculating affinity scores can be lengthy process depending on the size of your venue. Therefore, only one setup matching can be run at a time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect long runtimes for large venues; do not start multiple setup runs in parallel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching Group and computation/upload options
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Matching Group' is a dropdown of the groups you can use in the matcher (Reviewers, Area Chairs, Senior Area Chairs). You can select if you would like affinity scores and/or conflicts computed, or upload your own affinity scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatively, you can compute and upload your own affinity scores using the OpenReview expertise API. Directions for how to format uploaded scores are in the field description in the Paper Matching Setup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete and updated profiles requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: It is important that all Senior Area Chairs, Area Chairs, and Reviewers have a complete and updated Profile including their publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users can import publications from DBLP by editing their Profile. More complete and accurate Profile information will improve the quality of the affinity scores and conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior Area Chairs assignment modes and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Senior Area Chairs assignments can be done in two different ways: Senior Area Chairs are assigned submissions directly; or Senior Area Chairs are assigned to Area Chairs and the submissions assigned to their Area Chairs are assigned to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If assigned directly: this will compute affinity scores and conflicts between Senior Area Chairs and submissions. If assigned through Area Chairs: this will compute affinity scores between Senior Area Chairs and Area Chairs and conflicts between Senior Area Chairs and submissions. Assignments between Senior Area Chairs and Area Chairs must be done before starting matching between Area Chairs and submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area Chairs matching prerequisite when Senior ACs exist
rubrics_metrics.description: If your venue has Senior Area Chairs and you are performing Senior Area Chair assignments based on their Area Chairs, make sure that the Area Chairs already have assigned Senior Area Chairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is needed so that the Senior Area Chair conflicts are transferred to the Area Chairs too. Refer to the Senior Area Chairs section for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profile sections used for conflict detection
rubrics_metrics.description: Conflict detection uses the information of the users' coauthors from publications in OpenReview as long as they are publicly visible and the users' Profile. The sections of the Profile used for conflict detection are the Emails section, the Education & Career History section, and the Advisors, Relations & Conflicts section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Therefore, the more complete and accurate the information in the Profile is, the better the conflict detection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute Conflicts N Years parameter
rubrics_metrics.description: Another parameter that can be controlled is the amount of years you want to consider when looking at conflicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For example, if the amount of years is set to 5, only the history, relations and publications from the past 5 years will be taken into consideration. By default, all relations, history, and publications are taken into consideration for conflict detection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filter common email domains
rubrics_metrics.description: Since a lot of users use email services such as gmail.com, a list of common domains is used to filter them out before conflicts are computed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps avoid spurious domain-based conflicts caused by generic email providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default Information Extraction Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Default policy: Uses the domains and computes subdomains from the Education & Career History section; from the emails listed in the Advisors, Relations & Conflicts section; from the emails listed in the Emails section; and uses the publication ids in OpenReview that the user authored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy extracts domains/subdomains broadly from multiple Profile sections to detect institutional overlaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: NeurIPS Information Extraction Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: NeurIPS policy: Uses the domains and computes subdomains from the Education & Career History section (all intern positions are ignored); uses domains from the Advisors, Relations & Conflicts section only if the relation is that of a Coworker or a Coauthor; uses domains from the Emails section only if no domains were extracted from the Education & Career History and Advisors/Relations & Conflicts sections; uses the publication ids in OpenReview that the user authored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy addresses that emails do not have a range of dates and is more conservative about when to use email domains for conflict extraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for detecting conflicts between two users
rubrics_metrics.description: Once all the information is extracted from the users' Profiles, the following rules apply to find a conflict between User A and User B: (1) If any of the domains/subdomains from the Education & Career History section of user A matches at least one of the domains/subdomains of the same section of User B, then a conflict is detected. (2) If any of the domains/subdomains from the Advisors, Relations & Conflicts section or the Emails section of user A matches at least one of the domains/subdomains of the same sections of User B, then a conflict is detected. (3) If any of the publications of User A is the same as one of the publications of User B (coauthors), then a conflict is detected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the explicit matching rules the matcher applies after extracting domain/subdomain/publication information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Available affinity score models
rubrics_metrics.description: OpenReview has different models available to compute affinity scores between users and submissions. The current available models are: specter+mfr, specter2, scincl, specter+scincl.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you want to learn more about the models, you can find the open source repository referenced in the Paper Matching Setup page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upload affinity scores option
rubrics_metrics.description: You may also choose to upload your scores by selecting No (i.e., not compute via OpenReview).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directions for how to format uploaded scores are in the description of the field in the Paper Matching Setup. Alternatively use the OpenReview expertise API to generate scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling missing profiles during matching
rubrics_metrics.description: Running the paper matching setup should output a comment identifying members missing profiles or publications and will say 'Affinity scores and/or conflicts could not be computed for these users. Please ask these users to sign up in OpenReview and upload their papers. Alternatively, you can remove these users from the Reviewers group.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You have two options: remove reviewers without profiles from the reviewers group, or remind the reviewers that they need OpenReview profiles and wait for them to create them. You can run the Paper Matching Setup as many times as you want or until all users have completed profiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Email addresses vs profile IDs handling
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reviewer creates a profile, their email address will not be automatically updated to their profile ID in the reviewers' group. The matcher will still detect email addresses as users without profiles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any email addresses will either need to be removed or replaced with tilde IDs. This can be done automatically by re-running Paper Matching Setup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirming computed affinity scores
rubrics_metrics.description: You can confirm that the affinity scores were computed by checking if an invitation for the scores was created: https://api.openreview.net/edges?invitation=your/venue/id/role/-/Affinity_Score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Next, you should be able to run a paper matching from the ‘Paper Assignments’ link in your PC console after confirming the scores invitation exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Troubleshoot output messaging semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: The message identifying users without profiles does not mean that the process failed, but that those members were excluded from the calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret the setup output: lack of some users in calculations is expected unless you remove or fix those entries; you may re-run the setup after corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Runtime and procedural note about re-running
rubrics_metrics.description: You can run the Paper Matching Setup as many times as you want or until all users have completed profiles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because only one setup can run at a time and runs can be lengthy, coordinate runs with user profile updates to avoid redundant long jobs.
